quickSummary: Ploidy (n) represents chromosome number, while C-value represents nuclear DNA mass. In humans (2n=46): G1 has 46 chromosomes (2C). S-phase doubles DNA to 4C (92 chromatids) while chromosomes remain 2n=46. Mitotic anaphase temporarily has 92 chromosomes (4n, 4C) as centromeres split. Meiosis I separates homologues to produce cells with n=23 chromosomes (2C). Anaphase II temporarily doubles chromosome count to 46 before cytokinesis yields 4 gametes with n=23 and 1C DNA mass.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: DNA doubles in S-phase (2C -> 4C). Chromosome count halves in Anaphase I (2n -> n). Sister chromatids separate in Anaphase II (2C -> C).

conceptBreakdown.content: Understanding the exact relationship between **chromosome number ($n$)** and **nuclear DNA mass ($C$)** is the cornerstone of solving quantitative genetics and cell division problems in NEST and INBO exams.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Numerical Calculations & Problem Solving Rules
conceptBreakdown.title: Numerical Calculations & Problem Solving Rules
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Rule 1**: Counting centromeres gives the exact chromosome number. Counting individual DNA strands/arms gives the chromatid count.
2. **Rule 2**: In S-phase, DNA replication doubles the mass ($2C \rightarrow 4C$), but creates attached sister chromatids, leaving the chromosome count ($2n$) constant.
3. **Rule 3**: In Anaphase of Mitosis and Anaphase II of Meiosis, splitting of centromeres temporarily doubles the apparent chromosome number within that single dividing cell before cytokinesis completes.
4. **Rule 4**: In Meiosis I, reduction occurs because whole duplicated chromosomes move to opposite poles ($2n, 4C \rightarrow 2 \times [n, 2C]$).
